_stopped_at_is: the runner's own last log line, 'STOP-FILE <path> present: no further cycle', which is the moment it decided to end. The PROCESS exit is bounded rather than invented: present at 18:13:30Z, last log line 18:33:06Z, absent at 18:53:36Z -- so it exited between 18:33:06Z and 18:53:36Z. No instrument on this box recorded the exact exit instant, and this field does not pretend one did.
_stop_was_at_a_job_boundary: 'STOP-FILE <path> present: ending after the current job (7 pairs done)', then the cycle record 'CYCLE sa 20261015T153409Z ... stopped stopped_by_operator completed false'. Never killed; the task was not touched until the Disable.

_census.why_the_filter_is_narrow: MY FIRST PROBE MATCHED ANY COMMAND LINE CONTAINING THE TOKEN cycle_runner, and its own bash wrapper contained that token -- so it counted ITSELF and could never reach 0. Left armed it would have reported RUNNER-STILL-UP-AFTER-2H about a runner that had already exited, and that false ARMED row is what the narrow filter and the positive control prevent. Row NFRA_OPLGTW-Z-S152.
